methodology: Two INDEPENDENT short-window samples (one from the background census agent, ~2-4 minute window; one from the orchestrating session directly, 35.9-second window) were each projected to a daily HARD UPPER BOUND assuming unrealistic constant peak rate. The larger of the two bounds per file is reported as the conservative worst case. This is explicitly NOT a realistic daily-rate estimate -- see caveats.

flex_complete_database.db.caveat: HARD UPPER BOUND assuming unrealistic constant peak write rate 24/7 -- real workloads are bursty (confirmed: flex_complete_database.db showed a ZERO delta in one 36-second window and a nonzero delta in the other, proving it is NOT continuously writing at a steady rate). Treat this as a safety-margin ceiling, not an expected value.

explicit_disclaimer: These figures are HARD BOUNDS derived from two single short observation windows (36 seconds and ~2-4 minutes), NOT a measured daily rate. A real forecast requires observation across at least a full day-night cycle to capture realistic write cadence (batch jobs, scheduler cycles, quiet periods). Do not treat 'days to threshold' as a committed timeline -- it is a worst-case safety margin only, likely far more conservative (i.e. pessimistic) than reality, given flex_complete_database.db showed literally zero growth in one of the two sampled windows.
recommendation: A P1.5/P2 follow-up should run storage_monitor.take_snapshot() on an hourly cron for at least 48-72 hours before committing to any specific automated retention cadence -- this P1 pass could not responsibly extrapolate a real daily rate from two short bursts.
